I'm checking the user story against the quality criteria: it's a single objective, so the atomicity check passes, and I see no parenthetical notes that would break minimality.

Next I'm weighing the remaining criteria: the statement's justification is fine, no technology is imposed, and the vague-term check looks clean, though the unspecified download format and which data the receipt contains are open questions. Since there are no acceptance criteria, the story fails the estimability and testability checks.

I'm going through the remaining checks now: the story reads as a single, independent user-facing request with no conflicts or duplicates, and it follows the template. I'm still unsure whether it depends on an existing bill-payment feature, and I want to confirm that before settling the dependency check.

I'm running through the remaining checks: the story should be independent but doesn't mention its reliance on the payment record in the core system, so that dependency check fails. It's also not estimable, since the download format and the comprobante's contents are unspecified, and with no acceptance criteria it can't be verified. Size looks fine at a couple of points, and the non-functional check doesn't apply.

I'm checking whether downloading the receipt counts as a sensitive operation; it reads data rather than changing anything, so the authentication rule doesn't apply. The receipt likely shows account numbers, though, so the masking rule applies, and since the story doesn't define how those numbers should be masked, that check fails as a blocker.

I'm checking the remaining operational-security items: this download only reads data and doesn't change the session or the device settings, so the session rule doesn't apply. The receipt-masking check is still a blocker, and the file being saved to the device doesn't clash with any control the story states, so that check passes. I'm now moving on to the audit requirement for this operation.

I'm checking the accessibility item now: the story asks for a download action in the app, which implies a new button or screen, so the accessibility criterion applies. The story doesn't mention accessibility at all, so I'm marking that as a minor defect rather than skipping it.

I'm checking the SUGEF item next: the comprobante is information the customer receives, so I need to decide whether that counts as a financial operation that triggers the rule.

I'm settling on the defect list now: DOR-001 and DOR-002 are major, INV-003 and BM-007 are major, INV-005 and BM-003 are blocking, and BM-006 is minor. I'll mark the story as returned for rework, with the estimate still to be confirmed.

recomendaciones.texto: Agregar criterios de aceptación observables, por ejemplo: con un pago de servicios existente, la app ofrece descargar su comprobante; el archivo contiene fecha, monto, servicio y número de referencia. Definir qué pasa si el pago no tiene comprobante disponible.
Definir el enmascarado de los datos sensibles que aparezcan en el comprobante (número de cuenta, identificación) y en el archivo descargado, por ejemplo mostrando la cuenta como ****1234.
Precisar el alcance: formato del comprobante (PDF, imagen u otro), datos que debe incluir, y si aplica a cualquier pago de servicios o solo a los realizados desde la app.
Definir los casos de error relevantes: comprobante no disponible, pago no encontrado o descarga fallida, con el mensaje que ve el cliente.
Nombrar la dependencia de datos: de qué sistema o servicio del core se obtiene la información del pago para generar el comprobante.
Definir el comportamiento sin conexión o con error del servicio durante la descarga, por ejemplo reintento o mensaje, sin cerrar la app.
Indicar que la nueva acción de descarga cumple accesibilidad (lector de pantalla, contraste, tamaño de texto) con WCAG 2.1 AA, o confirmar que la DoR del equipo la incluye por defecto.
